1.name: Qwen Image 2.1 TextImage2Image Turbo 7B (Current Default)
1.suitability_notes: Rank #1 (Current): Fast 8-step distilled 7B model with native 2K (1664x960) & 4-portrait <image1..4> support (~35s/image). Fast, though 8-step distillation (CFG=1.0) can occasionally simplify complex multi-person spatial prompts.

2.name: Qwen Image 2.1 TextImage2Image 7B (Full 40-Step Base Model)
2.suitability_notes: Rank #2 (Most Recommended Upgrade): Un-distilled 40-step base version of Qwen Image 2.1 with full Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG=4.0). Reuses your already-installed Qwen3-VL encoder & VAE; follows complex spatial/Venn layouts, eye/mouth rules, and facial likeness much more faithfully than #1 Turbo.

3.name: Flux 2 Klein 9B KV (4-Step Reference KV-Cached)
3.suitability_notes: Rank #3: 9B Flux 2 Klein model with dedicated Reference KV-Caching across denoising steps. Specifically engineered for multi-reference character consistency at high speed (4 steps).

4.name: Flux 2 Klein Base 9B (Full 30-Step Un-Distilled CFG=4.0)
4.suitability_notes: Rank #4: Full 30-step un-distilled 9B Flux 2 Klein with CFG=4.0. Stronger prompt adherence, anatomy, and multi-character separation than the 4-step distilled variants.

5.name: Flux 2 Klein 9B (4-Step Distilled Standard)
5.suitability_notes: Rank #5: Standard 4-step distilled 9B Flux 2 Klein using Qwen3-8B text encoder. Much stronger facial identity than the 4B Klein model while remaining very fast.

6.name: Flux 3 Image Klein Base 5.6B (Full 50-Step CFG=3.5)
6.suitability_notes: Rank #6: Latest Flux 3 architecture with Qwen3-VL-4B vision-language encoder and native ordered <ref_image_0..3> reference conditioning (50 steps, CFG=3.5).

7.name: Flux 3 Image Klein 5.6B (16-Step Distilled)
7.suitability_notes: Rank #7: 16-step distilled Flux 3 Klein 5.6B with Qwen3-VL-4B vision-language encoder and ordered <ref_image_0..3> reference conditioning.

8.name: SenseNova U1.5 8B MoT (50-Step Unified VLM + Diffusion)
8.suitability_notes: Rank #8: 8B Mixture-of-Transformers architecture combining VLM understanding and image generation. Excels at complex spatial positioning, object counts, and multi-reference scenes.

9.name: Qwen Image Edit Plus (2511) 20B (40-Step Multi-Subject)
9.suitability_notes: Rank #9: Large 20B Qwen2.5-VL model tuned in release 2511 for combining multiple person references at 1664x960 with high identity retention. Slower on 8GB VRAM due to 20B size.

10.name: Fibo 2.0 Dev (50-Step Multi-Reference CFG=5.0)
10.suitability_notes: Rank #10: 50-step Fibo 2.0 Dev using Qwen3-VL-4B encoder + Flux 2 VAE; supports up to 4 ordered reference images.

11.name: Fibo 2.0 Edit Turbo (4-Step Distilled Multi-Reference)
11.suitability_notes: Rank #11: Fast 4-step distilled variant of Fibo 2.0 supporting 4 ordered reference images.

12.name: Flux 2 Klein Base 4B (30-Step Un-Distilled CFG=4.0)
12.suitability_notes: Rank #12: 30-step un-distilled 4B Flux 2 Klein. Low VRAM footprint with better prompt adherence than the 4-step 4B model, though 7B/9B models hold faces better.

13.name: Flux 2 Klein 4B (4-Step Distilled — Already Installed)
13.suitability_notes: Rank #13: Already downloaded on disk. Very fast (~15s, 4 steps), good lighting/atmosphere, but 4B capacity can lose facial likeness in complex two-shots.

14.name: Flux 1 Kontext DreamOmni2 12B (25-Step Multimodal)

15.name: pi-FLUX.2 Dev 32B (4-Step Distilled Giant Model)

16.suitability_notes: Rank #16: Full 30-step 32B Flux 2 Dev model. Highest parameter count in Wan2GP, but very slow on 8GB VRAM due to 32B offloading.
